correctness.rationale: The classical least-squares centered quadratic stencil is (-3,12,17,12,-3)/35 and fixes constants. Every real vector decomposes into positive nested binary cuts modulo constants; the Gini pair sum is additive over such nested cuts, while postfilter Gini obeys the triangle inequality, so the exact operator norm is the maximum over nonempty binary masks. For each n=5,6,7,8 independent exact integer enumeration visited all (2^n−2) masks: totals 30,62,126,254=472 and fixed-cardinality maxima (110,180);(157,256,303);(204,338,414);(251,420,531,560). Quotients give sharp L_n=(6/7,101/105,69/70,251/245). The n≥8 impulse formula follows algebraically from five distinct nonzero entries and their 10 mutual variations: G_n(35S_ne0)=47n−125, G_n(e0)=n−1. Thus strict amplification for all n≥8 is proved without extrapolating finite cases. The triangle inequality over five shifts gives L_n≤47/35, attained only in the n→∞ supremum. Correctness is limited to the specified periodic, equal-mass Gini setting; per-size norms n≥9 are not claimed.
residual_risks: Finite exhaustion restricted to the four explicitly claimed base sizes; no claim of sharp per-size n≥9 norm.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge PASS for sharp Gini operator norms on short cyclic rings and the universal n=8 amplification boundary. Candan–Inan 2014 full primary article explicitly derives this same five-coefficient stencil (equation (4) and text p.205) but studies minimum-norm polynomial fit and implementation, not complete-pair Gini amplification. The related full Resultary three-tap Gini theorem establishes an exact norm for a positive averaging filter, not the signed five-tap SG multiplier; its cut variance identity cannot infer the present maxima. The exact 47/35 absolute coefficient sum is elementary and not claimed novel alone; the finite exact cut threshold and its analytical all-size witness are the meaningful new statements.
residual_risks: Older unindexed Gini/mean-difference operator norms under alternative dispersion terminology might exist; current positive-filter theory does not settle this signed filter.

source_inspections.title: An eight-site boundary for Gini stability of cyclic five-point Savitzky–Golay smoothing

checked_sources: Exact n≤8 classification and algebraic n≥8 expansion witness
value.rationale: The five-point Savitzky–Golay filter is widely used to reduce measurement noise but has negative outer weights, so a global pairwise-dispersion contraction property is not automatic. Exactly locating the eight-site transition, with all-real-input proof and sharp family-wide amplification envelope, is a meaningful natural stability boundary for an established operator, not just a rederived coefficient stencil or arbitrary finite table.
residual_risks: Restricted to equal-sample periodic wraparound five-tap quadratic filter; no open-interval endpoints or multistep stability treated.

limitations: Finite norms known exactly through n=8; for n≥9 claim only strict lower bound and sharp family supremum, not exact individual norms.
Assumes periodic real data and uniform pair weights.
